_comment: Scenario-staged routing demo beside impassable terrain: a brittle player cavalry unit (60 mounts at morale 0.5) starts just west of the default hill (Rect2(1150, 380, 250, 200)) and holds there until an enemy cavalry charge from its WESTERN flank comes in. Both units stand clear of the hill for the whole clip: the router's block is 280 wu wide, so its centre at x=960 keeps its eastern file 50 wu clear of the hill's west face. The pursuer's target sits 190 wu west of the hill and 40 wu below its bottom edge, so its leg is clear of the hill and it charges straight east. Measured with a 2-tick dense state dump: the router holds at its spawn through tick 120, the charge makes contact at tick 159 and drives the router back about 60 wu west, the two fight one unbroken melee, and the router routs at tick 344. The rout keeps the router's slot grid where its men stood when it broke (#1765). Still in contact, it turns its heading off the melee (-157 degrees) onto its flight north at the bounded rate every flight turn uses (#1785), and while its front ranks are still in the melee (from the rout until it leaves contact at tick 544) its men run at the flight's pace, none held back as an engaged front, so its grid never swings round under them: it has turned to -154 degrees by tick 400, -144 by tick 480 and -131 by tick 560, and its mean body-to-slot gap stays between about 13 and 45 wu from the rout to the rally (19.8 wu at tick 343). On main bb2a9e4f the in-contact turn snapped, unfolded, and the gap went to 288.9 wu at tick 344 and 312.8 at tick 352. It flees north, drifting slightly east, past the hill's west face with the pursuer's files still among its own (about (934, 611) at tick 400, (945, 553) at tick 480, (955, 446) at tick 560, (954, 176) at tick 680), every man clear of the hill, and rallies at tick 704 (ROUTING at 703, IDLE at 704) at about (952, 109), inside the clip (it ends at tick 720). It pulls up with its men in step and its heading held where its flight turn had reached (-110 degrees, 20 degrees off its flight line, #1812): anchor about (952, 92) at tick 710, still coasting at about (951, 64) when the clip ends, so the rally's heading turn and re-square, which wait for the coast to stop, fall after the clip. The gap is 44.9 wu at tick 702 (86.7 on main bb2a9e4f). Its men's centroid has moved 10 wu 60 ticks after tick 342, 71 wu after 150 and 334 wu after 300 (main: 10, 64 and 292). The pursuer's facing turns smoothly through the charge, with no snap larger than 20 degrees between 2-tick samples. This scenario does NOT show a rout detouring around the hill. The 'stands and fights when genuinely trapped' case is covered by test_trapped_routing_unit_fights_instead_of_fleeing. No player input needed; the scenario + seed make the clash deterministic. After the rout the pursuer holds its facing (23.5 degrees) and its slot grid, FIGHTING, while the router runs north through and beside its files. At tick 530, as the router leaves contact, it re-faces 101 degrees to -77 (past the 75 degree threshold, so folded into its grid; mean body-to-slot gap 41.8 wu at tick 520, 38.7 at tick 530) and rides north after the router (about (945, 358) at tick 680). A 2-tick scan from the divergence (tick 343) reads its sustained shape residual at 27.9 wu, under the 30 wu threshold. On main bb2a9e4f the router streamed out through the pursuer's column eastward instead, the pursuer's facing snapped 35 degrees unfolded at tick 483 (#1806), and it stalled by the hill's south-west corner with a residual of 102.6 wu; that story no longer occurs here, so this clip no longer shows that snap. The declared checks pin the router's story beats with sparse post-rout samples (400, 560, 680, the rally at 703/704, and 710) rather than sampling the gallop densely. The router's own scramble (judged only on the 16 ticks after its rally) is declared below as an exemption rather than sampled around.

shape_residual.reason: uid 0 (the router): it rallies at tick 704, and the 16 ticks to the clip's end are its only judged samples (a router is not judged). Through them it coasts with its heading held where its flight turn had reached (-110 degrees), and its re-square waits for the coast to stop, after the clip, so its men stand about 41 to 45 wu off their slots on average (45.1 wu at tick 704, 41.2 at tick 720). That is the bounded flight turn's lag (the anchor runs along the flight line while the heading and grid turn behind it), not a scramble: the gap stays between about 13 and 45 wu from the rout on. Sustained shape residual 44.6 wu on 2-tick samples from the divergence (tick 343), against 69.7 wu on main bb2a9e4f, where the in-contact flight snap swung the grid under the men. The residual left is the deep router's slow bounded flight turn, which leaves it rallying 20 degrees off its flight line, and the rally re-square falling after the clip (#1812). Measured 2026-10-11.
